method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited text from the seat of the individual to whom the law is applied, with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18 and the writing-l4-rules skill; the duties with deadlines in s 347(3) and reg 4.31B(2) are regulative rules (PARTY ... MUST ... WITHIN ... LEST BREACH ... BECAUSE) run inside plain-fact questions; no REFUSE (gaps answer NOTHING or a `not covered` value, asserted); every satisfaction, belief, consideration, assessment or determination of the Minister, ASIO or the ART asked as an input; checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset. A layer beside baseline-2026-10 and naive-2026-10, which are untouched. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate.

focus: asylum seeker matters (the provisions a claimant meets)
scope: From the asylum seeker's seat (a non-citizen in Australia claiming protection, applying for a protection visa, seeking ART review, facing removal). Act: s 5AAA; s 5AA(1), (1A), (3); ss 5H, 5J, 5L, 5LA, 5M; s 36(1A)-(6); s 36A; s 46A(1), (1A), (2); ss 48A, 48B(1); ss 91C, 91D(1), 91E, 91F(1); ss 91J, 91K, 91L(1); s 91V(1)-(3); ss 91W, 91WA, 91WB; s 197C(1)-(3), (7A), (9); s 197D(6); ss 338A, 347(3), (5), 347A(4), (5), 348(1); s 368(7); ss 379A, 379C(2)-(5); ss 494B, 494C(2)-(6). Regulations: reg 2.16(3); reg 4.31B. Out: s 5K; Schedule 2 protection visa subclass criteria; reg 1.12; s 197C(4)-(7) and s 36A record (asked as facts); Part 5 procedure and remittal (s 349, reg 4.33); s 500; s 501; detention and removal duties (ss 189-198); ministerial intervention; s 46B; s 91G; ss 91X, 91Y; Parliament statements and personal-exercise machinery; ss 494C(7), 379C(7), 494D, 379G; fee indexation (regs 4.31BA, 4.31BB: an input).
seat: the asylum seeker (a non-citizen in Australia who claims protection: the protection visa applicant, the person whose protection visa is refused or cancelled and who seeks ART review, and the person facing removal)
